subs.title: De Moivre's Theorem and Roots of Unity
Geometry of Complex Numbers and Loci

questions.q: The smallest \(+\)ve integer \(n\) for which \(\left(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^n=1\) is :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}=i\) and \(i^n=1\) first at \(n=4\), which is not among (a)–(c).

questions.q: The complex numbers \(z=x+iy\) which satisfy the equation \(\left|\dfrac{z-5i}{z+5i}\right|=1\) lie on
opts: the circle passing through the origin
questions.sol: \(|z-5i|=|z+5i|\): \(z\) is equidistant from \(5i\) and \(-5i\), i.e. on their perpendicular bisector, the real axis.

questions.q: If \(z=\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}2+\dfrac i2\right)^5+\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}2-\dfrac i2\right)^5\) then
The inequality \(|z-4|<|z-2|\) represents the region given by
questions.sol: \(z\) is nearer to \(4\) than to \(2\): \((x-4)^2<(x-2)^2\) gives \(x>3\), i.e. \(\text{Re}(z)>3\), which is none of (a)–(c). (The book key prints (c).)

questions.q: If \(z=x+iy\) and \(w=\dfrac{1-iz}{z-i}\) then \(|w|=1\) implies that, in the complex plane :
questions.sol: \(|1-iz|=|-i||z+i|=|z+i|\), so \(|z+i|=|z-i|\): \(z\) is equidistant from \(\pm i\), i.e. on the real axis.

questions.q: The points \(z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4\) in the complex plane are the vertices of a parallelogram if and only if
questions.sol: The diagonals \(z_1z_3\) and \(z_2z_4\) bisect each other: \(\dfrac{z_1+z_3}2=\dfrac{z_2+z_4}2\).

questions.q: If \(a,b,c\); \(u,v,w\) are complex numbers representing the vertices of two triangles such that \(c=(1-r)a+rb\), \(w=(1-r)u+rv\) where \(r\) is a complex number, the two triangles :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{c-a}{b-a}=r=\dfrac{w-u}{v-u}\): the sides at \(a\) and \(u\) are in the same ratio and include equal angles, so the triangles are similar.

questions.q: If \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) are two non-zero complex numbers such that \(|z_1+z_2|=|z_1|+|z_2|\), then \(\text{Arg}\,z_1-\text{Arg}\,z_2\) is equal to
questions.sol: Equality in the triangle inequality holds only when \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) point in the same direction.

questions.q: The value of \(\sum\limits_{k=1}^6\left(\sin\dfrac{2\pi k}7-i\cos\dfrac{2\pi k}7\right)\) is
questions.sol: The sum is \(-i\sum\limits_{k=1}^6e^{2\pi ik/7}=-i(-1)=i\), since the seven \(7\)th roots of unity add to \(0\).

questions.q: The complex number \(\sin x+i\cos2x\) and \(\cos x-i\sin2x\) are conjugate to each other, for
questions.sol: Need \(\sin x=\cos x\) and \(\cos2x=\sin2x\), i.e. \(\tan x=1\) and \(\tan2x=1\). But \(\tan x=1\) makes \(\tan2x\) undefined. No value.

questions.q: If \(\omega(\ne1)\) is a cube root of unity and \((1+\omega)^7=A+B\omega\) then \(A\) and \(B\) are respectively
Let \(z\) and \(\omega\) be two non zero complex numbers such that \(|z|=|\omega|\) and \(\text{Arg}\,z+\text{Arg}\,\omega=\pi\), then \(z\) equals
questions.sol: With \(\omega=re^{i\theta}\): \(z=re^{i(\pi-\theta)}=-re^{-i\theta}=-\bar\omega\).

questions.q: Let \(z\) and \(\omega\) be two complex numbers such that \(|z|\le1\), \(|\omega|\le1\) and \(|z+i\omega|=|z-i\bar\omega|=2\) then \(z\) equals
questions.sol: \(2=|z+i\omega|\le|z|+|\omega|\le2\) forces \(|z|=|\omega|=1\) and \(z=i\omega\). Then \(i\bar\omega=-\bar z\), so \(|z+\bar z|=2|\text{Re}\,z|=2\) and \(z=\pm1\).

questions.q: For positive integers \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) the values of the expression \((1+i)^{n_1}+(1+i^3)^{n_1}+(1+i^5)^{n_2}+(1+i^7)^{n_2}\) when \(i=\sqrt{-1}\) is real if and only if
questions.sol: The expression is \(\left[(1+i)^{n_1}+(1-i)^{n_1}\right]+\left[(1+i)^{n_2}+(1-i)^{n_2}\right]\); each bracket is a number plus its conjugate, hence real for all positive \(n_1,n_2\).

questions.q: If \(\omega\) is an imaginary cube roots of unity, then \((1+\omega-\omega^2)^7\) equals
questions.sol: \(1+\omega=-\omega^2\), so the number is \((-2\omega^2)^7=-128\omega^{14}=-128\omega^2\).

questions.q: The value of the sum \(\sum\limits_{n=1}^{13}(i^n+i^{n+1})\), where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\) equals
questions.sol: \((1+i)\sum\limits_{n=1}^{13}i^n=(1+i)\cdot i=i-1\) (four consecutive powers of \(i\) add to \(0\), leaving \(i^{13}=i\)).

questions.q: If \(i=\sqrt{-1}\), then \(4+5\left(\dfrac{-1}2+\dfrac{i\sqrt3}2\right)^{334}+3\left(\dfrac{-1}2+\dfrac{i\sqrt3}2\right)^{365}\) is equal to
questions.sol: With \(\omega=\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}2\): \(\omega^{334}=\omega\), \(\omega^{365}=\omega^2\). \(4+5\omega+3\omega^2=1+2\omega+3(1+\omega+\omega^2)=1+2\omega=i\sqrt3\).

questions.q: If \(\arg(z)<0\), then \(\arg(-z)-\arg(z)=\)
questions.sol: For \(\arg z=\theta\in(-\pi,0)\), \(-z\) has principal argument \(\theta+\pi\). The difference is \(\pi\). (The book key prints (b).)

questions.q: If \(z_1,z_2,z_3\) are complex numbers such that \(|z_1|=|z_2|=|z_3|=1\), \(\left|\dfrac1{z_1}+\dfrac1{z_2}+\dfrac1{z_3}\right|=1\), then \(|z_1+z_2+z_3|\) is
questions.sol: \(|z_k|=1\) gives \(\dfrac1{z_k}=\bar z_k\), so \(1=|\bar z_1+\bar z_2+\bar z_3|=|z_1+z_2+z_3|\).

questions.q: Let \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) be \(n^{th}\) roots of unity which subtend a right angle at the origin, then '\(n\)' must be of the form
questions.sol: Arguments of \(n\)th roots differ by multiples of \(\dfrac{2\pi}n\): \(\dfrac{2\pi m}n=\dfrac\pi2\) gives \(n=4m\).

questions.q: The complex number \(z_1,z_2\) and \(z_3\) satisfying \(\dfrac{z_1-z_3}{z_2-z_3}=\dfrac{1-i\sqrt3}2\) are the vertices of the triangle which is
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1-i\sqrt3}2=e^{-i\pi/3}\): \(|z_1-z_3|=|z_2-z_3|\) and the angle at \(z_3\) is \(60^\circ\), so the triangle is equilateral.

questions.q: Let \(\omega=-\dfrac12+i\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\). Then the value of \(\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&-1-\omega^2&\omega^2\\1&\omega^2&\omega^4\end{vmatrix}\)
questions.sol: \(-1-\omega^2=\omega\) and \(\omega^4=\omega\). The determinant \(\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&\omega&\omega^2\\1&\omega^2&\omega\end{vmatrix}=(\omega^2-\omega^4)-(\omega-\omega^2)+(\omega^2-\omega)=3\omega^2-3\omega\).

questions.q: For all complex numbers \(z_1,z_2\) satisfying \(|z_1|=12\) and \(|z_2-3-4i|=5\), the minimum value of \(|z_1-z_2|\) is
questions.sol: The circle \(|z-3-4i|=5\) passes through the origin and lies inside \(|z|=12\); its farthest point from \(O\) is at distance \(10\). Minimum gap \(=12-10=2\).

questions.q: If \(|z|=1\) and \(\omega=\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}\) (where \(z\ne-1\)), then \(\text{Re}(\omega)\) is
questions.sol: \(\omega=\dfrac{(z-1)(\bar z+1)}{|z+1|^2}=\dfrac{|z|^2-1+(z-\bar z)}{|z+1|^2}\); with \(|z|=1\) the numerator \(z-\bar z\) is purely imaginary.

questions.q: If \(\omega(\ne1)\) be a cube root of unity and \((1+\omega^2)^n=(1+\omega^4)^n\), then the least positive value of \(n\) is
questions.sol: \((-\omega)^n=(-\omega^2)^n\) gives \(\omega^n=1\), least \(n=3\).

questions.q: \(PQ\) and \(PR\) are two infinite rays, \(QAR\) is an arc. Point lying in the shaded region excluding the boundary satisfies
questions.sol: \(PQ=PR=PA=2\), so the arc is part of the circle \(|z+1|=2\) centred at \(P(-1,0)\), and the rays \(PQ\), \(PR\) make angles \(\pm\dfrac\pi4\) with the real axis. The shaded region is outside the circle and between the rays.

questions.q: The minimum value of \(|a+b\omega+c\omega^2|\), where \(a,b\) and \(c\) are all not equal integers and \((\omega\ne1)\) is a cube root of unity, is
questions.sol: \(|a+b\omega+c\omega^2|^2=\tfrac12\left[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\right]\). Not all equal: the least value is with two equal and the third differing by \(1\): \(\tfrac12(0+1+1)=1\).

questions.q: If \(x,y,z\) are real and distinct then \(u=x^2+4y^2+9z^2-6yz-3zx-2xy\) is always
If \(\dfrac{\omega-\bar\omega z}{1-z}\) is purely real where \(\omega=\alpha+i\beta\), \(\beta\ne0\) and \(z\ne1\), then the set of the values of \(z\) is
questions.sol: Equate the number to its conjugate: \((\omega-\bar\omega z)(1-\bar z)=(\bar\omega-\omega\bar z)(1-z)\), which simplifies to \((\omega-\bar\omega)(1-|z|^2)=0\). As \(\omega\ne\bar\omega\): \(|z|=1\), with \(z\ne1\).

questions.q: A man walks a distance of \(3\) units from the origin towards the north-east (N \(45^\circ\) E) direction. From there, he walks a distance of \(4\) units towards the north-west (N \(45^\circ\) W) direction to reach a point \(P\). Then the position of \(P\) in the Argand plane is
If \(|z|=1\) and \(z\ne\pm1\), then all the values of \(\dfrac z{1-z^2}\) lie on
opts: a line not passing through the origin
questions.sol: \(\dfrac z{1-z^2}=\dfrac1{\bar z-z}\) (as \(\frac1z=\bar z\)) \(=\dfrac1{-2i\,\text{Im}\,z}=\dfrac i{2\,\text{Im}\,z}\), purely imaginary.

questions.q: A particle \(P\) starts from the point \(z_0=1+2i\), where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). It moves first horizontally away from origin by \(5\) units and then vertically away from origin by \(3\) units to reach a point \(z_1\). From \(z_1\) the particle moves \(\sqrt2\) units in the direction of the vector \(\hat i+\hat j\) and then it moves through an angle \(\dfrac\pi2\) in anticlockwise direction on a circle with centre at origin, to reach a point \(z_2\). The point \(z_2\) is given by
Let \(z=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta\). Then the value of \(\sum\limits_{m=1}^{15}\text{Im}(z^{2m-1})\) at \(\theta=2^\circ\) is
questions.sol: \(\sum\limits_{m=1}^{15}\sin(2m-1)\theta=\dfrac{\sin^215\theta}{\sin\theta}=\dfrac{\sin^230^\circ}{\sin2^\circ}=\dfrac1{4\sin2^\circ}\).

questions.q: Let \(z=x+iy\) be a complex number where \(x\) and \(y\) are integers. Then the area of the rectangle whose vertices are the roots of the equation \(z\bar z^3+\bar zz^3=350\) is
Let \(z\) be a complex number such that the imaginary part of \(z\) is nonzero and \(a=z^2+z+1\) is real. Then \(a\) cannot take the value
questions.sol: \(z^2+z+(1-a)=0\) has real coefficients and a non-real root, so \(1-4(1-a)<0\), i.e. \(a<\dfrac34\).

questions.q: Let complex numbers \(\alpha\) and \(\dfrac1{\bar\alpha}\) lie on circles \((x-x_0)^2+(y-y_0)^2=r^2\) and \((x-x_0)^2+(y-y_0)^2=4r^2\), respectively. If \(z_0=x_0+iy_0\) satisfies the equation \(2|z_0|^2=r^2+2\), then \(|\alpha|=\)
questions.sol: \(|\alpha-z_0|^2=r^2\) gives \(2\text{Re}(\alpha\bar z_0)=|\alpha|^2+|z_0|^2-r^2\). \(\left|\frac1{\bar\alpha}-z_0\right|^2=4r^2\) gives \(1+|\alpha|^2|z_0|^2-2\text{Re}(\alpha\bar z_0)=4r^2|\alpha|^2\). Eliminating: \((|\alpha|^2-1)(|z_0|^2-1)+r^2=4r^2|\alpha|^2\). With \(|z_0|^2-1=\frac{r^2}2\): \(|\alpha|^2+1=8|\alpha|^2\).

questions.q: Let \(S\) be the set of all complex numbers \(z\) satisfying \(|z-2+i|\ge\sqrt5\). If the complex number \(z_0\) is such that \(\dfrac1{|z_0-1|}\) is the maximum of the set \(\left\{\dfrac1{|z-1|}:z\in S\right\}\), then the principal argument of \(\dfrac{4-z_0-\bar z_0}{z_0-\bar z_0+2i}\) is
questions.sol: \(1\) lies inside the circle (centre \(2-i\), radius \(\sqrt5\)); the nearest point of \(S\) is on the ray from the centre through \(1\): \(z_0=2-i+\sqrt{\tfrac52}(-1+i)\). With \(k=\sqrt{\tfrac52}\): \(4-2\text{Re}\,z_0=2k\) and \(2i\,\text{Im}\,z_0+2i=2ik\). Ratio \(=\dfrac1i=-i\).

questions.q:
Let \(\theta_1,\theta_2,\ldots,\theta_{10}\) be positive valued angles (in radian) such that \(\theta_1+\theta_2+\ldots+\theta_{10}=2\pi\). Define the complex numbers \(z_1=e^{i\theta_1}\), \(z_k=z_{k-1}e^{i\theta_k}\) for \(k=2,3,\ldots,10\), where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). Consider the statements \(P\) and \(Q\) given below :
\(P:|z_2-z_1|+|z_3-z_2|+\ldots+|z_{10}-z_9|+|z_1-z_{10}|\le2\pi\)
\(Q:|z_2^2-z_1^2|+|z_3^2-z_2^2|+\ldots+|z_{10}^2-z_9^2|+|z_1^2-z_{10}^2|\le4\pi\)
Then,
questions.sol: The points lie on the unit circle; each chord \(|z_k-z_{k-1}|\) is at most its arc \(\theta_k\), and the arcs total \(2\pi\): \(P\) is true. \(|z_k^2-z_{k-1}^2|=|z_k-z_{k-1}||z_k+z_{k-1}|\le2|z_k-z_{k-1}|\), so the second sum is \(\le4\pi\): \(Q\) is true.

questions.q: If \(z_1=a+ib\) and \(z_2=c+id\) are complex numbers such that \(|z_1|=|z_2|=1\) and \(\text{Re}(z_1\bar z_2)=0\), then the pair of complex numbers \(w_1=a+ic\) and \(w_2=b+id\) satisfies :
questions.sol: Take \(a=\cos\alpha\), \(b=\sin\alpha\), \(c=\cos\beta\), \(d=\sin\beta\) with \(\cos(\alpha-\beta)=0\). Then \(\cos^2\beta=\sin^2\alpha\), so \(a^2+c^2=1\) and \(b^2+d^2=1\). \(\text{Re}(w_1\bar w_2)=ab+cd=\tfrac12(\sin2\alpha+\sin2\beta)=\sin(\alpha+\beta)\cos(\alpha-\beta)=0\).

questions.q: Let \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) be complex numbers such that \(z_1\ne z_2\) and \(|z_1|=|z_2|\). If \(z_1\) has positive real number part and \(z_2\) has negative imaginary part, then \(\dfrac{z_1+z_2}{z_1-z_2}\) may be
questions.sol: With \(|z_1|=|z_2|\): \(\dfrac{z_1+z_2}{z_1-z_2}=-i\cot\dfrac{\theta_1-\theta_2}2\), which is purely imaginary, or zero when \(z_2=-z_1\) (e.g. \(z_1=1+i\), \(z_2=-1-i\)). So it may be zero or (purely imaginary) none of these.

questions.q: Let \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) be two distinct complex numbers and let \(z=(1-t)z_1+tz_2\) for some real number \(t\) with \(0<t<1\). If \(\text{Arg}(\omega)\) denotes the principal argument of a non-zero complex number \(\omega\), then
questions.sol: \(z\) lies on the segment between \(z_1\) and \(z_2\), so (a) holds. \(z-z_1=t(z_2-z_1)\) with \(t>0\): (d) holds, and the rows of the determinant are proportional: (c). \(z-z_2=-(1-t)(z_2-z_1)\) points the opposite way: (b) fails.

questions.q: Let \(w=\dfrac{\sqrt3+i}2\) and \(P=\{w^n:n=1,2,3,\ldots\}\). Further \(H_1=\left\{z\in C:\text{Re}\,z>\dfrac12\right\}\) and \(H_2=\left\{z\in C:\text{Re}\,z<-\dfrac12\right\}\), where \(C\) is the set of all complex numbers. If \(z_1\in P\cap H_1\), \(z_2\in P\cap H_2\) and \(O\) represents the origin, then \(\angle z_1Oz_2=\)
questions.sol: \(w=e^{i\pi/6}\), so \(P\) is the set of \(12\)th roots of unity. \(P\cap H_1\): arguments \(0,\pm\frac\pi6\); \(P\cap H_2\): arguments \(\pi,\pm\frac{5\pi}6\). Possible angles: \(\frac{2\pi}3,\frac{5\pi}6,\pi\).

questions.q: Let \(\omega\) be a complex cube root of unity with \(\omega\ne1\) and \(P=[p_{ij}]\) be a \(n\times n\) matrix with \(p_{ij}=\omega^{i+j}\). Then \(P^2\ne0\), when \(n=\)
questions.sol: \((P^2)_{ij}=\omega^{i+j}\sum\limits_{k=1}^n\omega^{2k}\), and \(\sum\limits_{k=1}^n\omega^{2k}=0\) exactly when \(n\) is a multiple of \(3\). \(57\) is a multiple of \(3\); \(55,56,58\) are not.

questions.q: Let \(a,b\in R\) and \(a^2+b^2\ne0\). Suppose \(S=\left\{z\in C:z=\dfrac1{a+ibt},\ t\in R,\ t\ne0\right\}\), where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). If \(z=x+iy\) and \(z\in S\), then \((x,y)\) lies on
opts: the circle with radius \(\dfrac1{2a}\) and centre \(\left(\dfrac1{2a},0\right)\) for \(a>0\), \(b\ne0\)
the circle with radius \(-\dfrac1{2a}\) and centre \(\left(-\dfrac1{2a},0\right)\) for \(a<0\), \(b\ne0\).
questions.sol: \(x=\dfrac a{a^2+b^2t^2}\), \(y=\dfrac{-bt}{a^2+b^2t^2}\), so \(x^2+y^2=\dfrac xa\) when \(a\ne0\), \(b\ne0\): a circle with centre \(\left(\frac1{2a},0\right)\) and radius \(\frac1{2|a|}\) — (a) is right, (b) has the wrong centre. \(b=0\): \(z=\frac1a\) is real; \(a=0\): \(z=\frac{-i}{bt}\) is imaginary.

questions.q: Let \(a,b,x\) and \(y\) be real numbers such that \(a-b=1\) and \(y\ne0\). If the complex number \(z=x+iy\) satisfies \(\text{Im}\left(\dfrac{az+b}{z+1}\right)=y\), then which of the following is (are) possible value (s) of \(x\)?
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{az+b}{z+1}=a-\dfrac{a-b}{z+1}=a-\dfrac1{z+1}\), whose imaginary part is \(\dfrac y{(x+1)^2+y^2}\). Equating to \(y\ne0\): \((x+1)^2+y^2=1\).

questions.q: For a non-zero complex number \(z\), let \(\arg(z)\) denote the principal argument with \(-\pi<\arg(z)\le\pi\). Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) FALSE?
opts: The function \(f:R\to(-\pi,\pi]\), defined by \(f(t)=\arg(-1+it)\) for all \(t\in R\), is continuous at all points of \(R\), where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\)
For any two non-zero complex numbers \(z_1\) and \(z_2\), \(\arg\left(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}\right)-\arg(z_1)+\arg(z_2)\) is an integer multiple of \(2\pi\).

For any three given distinct complex numbers \(z_1,z_2\) and \(z_3\), the locus of the point \(z\) satisfying the condition \(\arg\left(\dfrac{(z-z_1)(z_2-z_3)}{(z-z_3)(z_2-z_1)}\right)=\pi\), lies on a straight line.
questions.sol: (a) \(\arg(-1-i)=-\frac{3\pi}4\): false. (b) \(f(0)=\pi\) but \(f(t)\to-\pi\) as \(t\to0^-\): discontinuous, false. (c) true (arguments are equal modulo \(2\pi\)). (d) The condition makes \(z,z_1,z_2,z_3\) concyclic, so the locus lies on a circle: false.

questions.q: Let \(s,t,r\) be non-zero complex numbers and \(L\) be the set of solutions \(z=x+iy\) \((x,y\in R,\ i=\sqrt{-1})\) of the equation \(sz+t\bar z+r=0\), where \(\bar z=x-iy\). Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
opts: If \(L\) has exactly one element, then \(|s|\ne|t|\)
If \(|s|=|t|\), then \(L\) has infinitely many elements
The number of elements in \(L\cap\{z:|z-1+i|=5\}\) is at most \(2\)
If \(L\) has more than one element, then \(L\) has infinitely many elements
questions.sol: With the conjugate equation \(\bar t z+\bar s\bar z+\bar r=0\), eliminating \(\bar z\): \((|s|^2-|t|^2)z=t\bar r-r\bar s\). If \(|s|\ne|t|\) there is exactly one solution; if \(|s|=|t|\) the set is either empty or a whole line. So (a), (d) are true, (b) is false, and a point or a line meets a circle in at most \(2\) points (c).

questions.q: Let \(S\) be the set of all complex numbers \(z\) satisfying \(|z^2+z+1|=1\). Then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
opts: The set \(S\) has exactly four elements
questions.sol: With \(w=z+\frac12\): \(\left|w^2+\frac34\right|=1\), so \(\frac14\le|w|^2\le\frac74\). Hence \(|w|\ge\frac12\) (c), and \(|z|\le|w|+\frac12\le\frac{\sqrt7+1}2<2\) (b). \(S\) is a curve with infinitely many points.

questions.q: For any complex number \(w=c+id\), let \(\arg(w)\in(-\pi,\pi]\), where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be real numbers such that for all complex numbers \(z=x+iy\) satisfying \(\arg\left(\dfrac{z+\alpha}{z+\beta}\right)=\dfrac\pi4\), the ordered pair \((x,y)\) lies on the circle \(x^2+y^2+5x-3y+4=0\). Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
questions.sol: The arc ends at the real points \(-\alpha,-\beta\), which lie on the circle: \(x^2+5x+4=0\) gives \(\{\alpha,\beta\}=\{1,4\}\). The centre \(\left(-\frac52,\frac32\right)\) is above the axis, so the arc is the upper one; there \(\arg(z+1)>\arg(z+4)\), and \(\arg(z+\alpha)-\arg(z+\beta)=+\frac\pi4\) needs \(\alpha=1\), \(\beta=4\).

questions.q: Let \(\bar z\) denote the complex conjugate of a complex number \(z\). If \(z\) is a non-zero complex number for which both real and imaginary parts of \((\bar z)^2+\dfrac1{z^2}\) are integers, then which of the following is/are possible value(s) of \(|z|\)?
questions.sol: With \(z=re^{i\theta}\): \((\bar z)^2+\dfrac1{z^2}=\left(r^2+\dfrac1{r^2}\right)e^{-2i\theta}\), so \(\left(r^2+\frac1{r^2}\right)^2=m^2+n^2=N\) (integers \(m,n\)). Then \(r^4=\dfrac{N-2\pm\sqrt{N(N-4)}}2\). For (a): \(N=45=6^2+3^2\) and \(\sqrt{45\cdot41}=3\sqrt{205}\) ✓. In (b), (c), (d) \(N-2\) would be \(\frac72,\frac92,\frac73\) — not integers.

questions.q: If \(x+iy=\sqrt{\dfrac{a+ib}{c+id}}\) prove that \((x^2+y^2)^2=\dfrac{a^2+b^2}{c^2+d^2}\)
questions.sol: Squaring: \((x+iy)^2=\dfrac{a+ib}{c+id}\). Taking moduli: \(x^2+y^2=\dfrac{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}{\sqrt{c^2+d^2}}\); squaring again gives the result.

questions.q: If \(x=a+b\), \(y=a\alpha+b\beta\), \(z=a\beta+b\alpha\) where \(\alpha,\beta\) are complex cube roots of unity show that \(xyz=a^3+b^3\)
questions.sol: With \(\alpha=\omega\), \(\beta=\omega^2\): \(yz=a^2\omega^3+ab(\omega^2+\omega^4)+b^2\omega^3=a^2-ab+b^2\). So \(xyz=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)=a^3+b^3\).

questions.q: Express \(\dfrac1{(1-\cos\theta)+2i\sin\theta}\) in the form \(A+iB\).
questions.sol: Multiply by the conjugate: \(\dfrac{(1-\cos\theta)-2i\sin\theta}{(1-\cos\theta)^2+4\sin^2\theta}\). Numerator \(=2\sin\frac\theta2\left(\sin\frac\theta2-2i\cos\frac\theta2\right)\), denominator \(=4\sin^2\frac\theta2\left(1+3\cos^2\frac\theta2\right)\).

questions.q: Find the real values of \(x\) and \(y\) for which the following equation is satisfied : \(\dfrac{(1+i)x-2i}{3+i}+\dfrac{(2-3i)y+i}{3-i}=i\)
Let the complex numbers \(z_1,z_2\) and \(z_3\) be the vertices of an equilateral triangle. If \(z_0\) be the circumcentre of the triangle, then prove that \(z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2=3z_0^2\).
questions.sol: For an equilateral triangle \(z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2=z_1z_2+z_2z_3+z_3z_1\) and the circumcentre is the centroid: \(3z_0=z_1+z_2+z_3\). Squaring: \(9z_0^2=\sum z_1^2+2\sum z_1z_2=3\sum z_1^2\).

questions.q: A relation \(R\) on the set of complex numbers is defined by \(z_1Rz_2\) if and only if \(\dfrac{z_1-z_2}{z_1+z_2}\) is real show that \(R\) is an equivalence relation.
questions.sol: Reflexive: \(\frac{z-z}{2z}=0\) is real. Symmetric: \(\frac{z_2-z_1}{z_2+z_1}=-\frac{z_1-z_2}{z_1+z_2}\) is real. Transitive: \(\frac{z_1-z_2}{z_1+z_2}=k\) real gives \(\frac{z_1}{z_2}=\frac{1+k}{1-k}\) real; similarly \(\frac{z_2}{z_3}\) is real, so \(\frac{z_1}{z_3}\) is real and hence \(\frac{z_1-z_3}{z_1+z_3}\) is real.

questions.q: Prove that the complex numbers \(z_1,z_2\) and the origin form an equilateral triangle if and only if \(z_1^2+z_2^2-z_1z_2=0\)
questions.sol: The triangle \(O,z_1,z_2\) is equilateral iff \(z_2=z_1e^{\pm i\pi/3}\), i.e. iff \(w=\frac{z_2}{z_1}\) satisfies \(w^2-w+1=0\) (whose roots are \(e^{\pm i\pi/3}\)), i.e. iff \(z_1^2+z_2^2-z_1z_2=0\).

questions.q: If \(1,a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{n-1}\) are the \(n\) roots of unity then show that \((1-a_1)(1-a_2)\ldots(1-a_{n-1})=n\).
It is given that \(n\) is an odd integer greater than three, but \(n\) is not a multiple of \(3\). Prove that \(x^3+x^2+x\) is a factor of \((x+1)^n-x^n-1\).
questions.sol: \(x^3+x^2+x=x(x-\omega)(x-\omega^2)\). Let \(f(x)=(x+1)^n-x^n-1\). \(f(0)=0\). \(f(\omega)=(-\omega^2)^n-\omega^n-1=-(1+\omega^n+\omega^{2n})\) (\(n\) odd) \(=0\) as \(n\) is not a multiple of \(3\). Similarly \(f(\omega^2)=0\).

questions.q: Show that the area of the triangle on the argand diagram formed by the complex numbers, \(z\), \(iz\) and \(z+iz\) is \(\dfrac12|z|^2\).
questions.sol: From the vertex \(z+iz\) the sides to \(z\) and \(iz\) are \(-iz\) and \(-z\): both of length \(|z|\) and perpendicular. Area \(=\frac12|z|\cdot|z|\).

questions.q: Complex numbers \(z_1,z_2,z_3\) are the vertices \(A,B,C\) respectively of an isosceles right angled triangle with right angle at \(C\) show that \((z_1-z_2)^2=2(z_1-z_3)(z_3-z_2)\)
Let \(z_1=10+6i\) and \(z_2=4+6i\). If \(z\) is any complex number such that the argument of \((z-z_1)/(z-z_2)\) is \(\dfrac\pi4\), then prove that \(|z-7-9i|=3\sqrt2\)
If \(iz^3+z^2-z+i=0\) then show that \(|z|=1\)
Let \(z\) and \(\omega\) be two complex numbers such that \(|z|\le1\), \(|\omega|\le1\) then show that \(|z-\omega|^2\le(|z|-|\omega|)^2+(\text{Arg}\,z-\text{Arg}\,\omega)^2\)
questions.sol: With \(z=r_1e^{i\theta_1}\), \(\omega=r_2e^{i\theta_2}\): \(|z-\omega|^2=(r_1-r_2)^2+4r_1r_2\sin^2\dfrac{\theta_1-\theta_2}2\le(r_1-r_2)^2+(\theta_1-\theta_2)^2\), using \(r_1r_2\le1\) and \(|\sin t|\le|t|\).

questions.q: Find all non zero complex number \(z\) satisfying \(\bar z=iz^2\)
questions.sol: Moduli: \(|z|=|z|^2\), so \(|z|=1\) and \(\bar z=\frac1z\). Then \(z^3=\frac1i=-i\), giving \(z=e^{i\pi/2},\ e^{-i\pi/6},\ e^{7i\pi/6}\).

questions.q: Let \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) be roots of the equation, \(z^2+pz+q=0\), where the co-efficients \(p\) and \(q\) may be complex numbers. Let \(A\) and \(B\) represent \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) in the complex plane. If \(\angle AOB=\alpha\ne0\) and \(OA=OB\), where \(O\) is the origin, prove that \(p^2=4q\cos^2\left(\dfrac\alpha2\right)\).
questions.sol: \(z_2=z_1e^{i\alpha}\). \(p^2=(z_1+z_2)^2=z_1^2(1+e^{i\alpha})^2=z_1^2e^{i\alpha}\left(e^{i\alpha/2}+e^{-i\alpha/2}\right)^2=q\cdot4\cos^2\dfrac\alpha2\), as \(q=z_1z_2=z_1^2e^{i\alpha}\).

questions.q: Prove that \(\sum\limits_{k=1}^{n-1}(n-k)\cos\dfrac{2k\pi}n=-\dfrac n2\), where \(n\ge3\) is an integer.
questions.sol: Let \(S\) be the sum. Replacing \(k\) by \(n-k\): \(S=\sum\limits_{k=1}^{n-1}k\cos\dfrac{2k\pi}n\). Adding: \(2S=n\sum\limits_{k=1}^{n-1}\cos\dfrac{2k\pi}n=n(-1)\), since the real parts of all \(n\)th roots of unity add to \(0\).

questions.q: Let \(\bar bz+b\bar z=c\), \(b\ne0\), be a line in the complex plane, where \(\bar b\) is the complex conjugate of \(b\), if a point \(z_1\) is the reflection of a point \(z_2\) through the line, then show that, \(c=\bar z_1b+z_2\bar b\)
questions.sol: The mid-point lies on the line: \(\bar b(z_1+z_2)+b(\bar z_1+\bar z_2)=2c\). The line has normal direction \(b\), so \(z_1-z_2=\lambda b\) (\(\lambda\) real), giving \(\bar b(z_1-z_2)=b(\bar z_1-\bar z_2)\), i.e. \(\bar bz_1+b\bar z_2=b\bar z_1+\bar bz_2\). Substituting in the first relation: \(2(b\bar z_1+\bar bz_2)=2c\).

questions.q: For complex numbers \(z\) and \(\omega\), prove that \(|z|^2\omega-|\omega|^2z=z-\omega\) if and only if \(z=\omega\) or \(z\bar\omega=1\).
questions.sol: The equation is \(z(1+|\omega|^2)=\omega(1+|z|^2)\), so \(z=k\omega\) with \(k>0\) real. Then \(k(1+|\omega|^2)=1+k^2|\omega|^2\), i.e. \((k-1)(1-k|\omega|^2)=0\): \(k=1\) (\(z=\omega\)) or \(k|\omega|^2=1\) (\(z\bar\omega=1\)). Conversely both cases satisfy the equation on substitution.

questions.q: Let a complex number \(\alpha\), \(\alpha\ne1\) be a root of the equation \(z^{p+q}-z^p-z^q+1=0\), when \(p,q\) are distinct primes. Show that either \(1+\alpha+\alpha^2+\ldots+\alpha^{p-1}=0\) or \(1+\alpha+\alpha^2+\ldots+\alpha^{q-1}=0\), but not both together.
questions.sol: \((z^p-1)(z^q-1)=0\), so \(\alpha^p=1\) or \(\alpha^q=1\); since \(\alpha\ne1\), \(\dfrac{\alpha^p-1}{\alpha-1}=0\) or \(\dfrac{\alpha^q-1}{\alpha-1}=0\). If both held, \(\alpha^p=\alpha^q=1\) with \(\gcd(p,q)=1\) would give \(\alpha=1\), a contradiction.

questions.q: If \(z_1\) & \(z_2\) are two complex numbers such that \(|z_1|<1<|z_2|\) then prove that \(\left|\dfrac{1-z_1\bar z_2}{z_1-z_2}\right|<1\).
Prove that there exists no complex number \(z\) such that \(|z|<\dfrac13\) and \(\sum\limits_{r=1}^na_rz^r=1\) where \(|a_r|<2\).
questions.sol: \(\left|\sum a_rz^r\right|\le\sum|a_r||z|^r<2\sum\limits_{r=1}^n\left(\dfrac13\right)^r<2\cdot\dfrac{1/3}{1-1/3}=1\), so the sum cannot equal \(1\).

questions.q: \(|z-1|=\sqrt2\) is a circle inscribed in a square whose one vertex is \(2+i\sqrt3\). Find the remaining vertex.
questions.sol: The centre is \(1\) and the vertex is at \(1+(1+i\sqrt3)\). Rotating \(1+i\sqrt3\) about the centre by \(90^\circ\) repeatedly (multiplying by \(i\)): \(-\sqrt3+i\), \(-1-i\sqrt3\), \(\sqrt3-i\). Adding the centre \(1\) gives the other vertices.

questions.q: For complex number \(z_1=x_1+iy_1\) and \(z_2=x_2+iy_2\), we write \(z_1\cap z_2\), if \(x_1\le x_2\) and \(y_1\le y_2\). Then for all complex numbers \(z\) with \(1\cap z\), we have \(\dfrac{1-z}{1+z}\cap0\).
questions.sol: \(z=x+iy\) with \(x\ge1\), \(y\ge0\). \(\dfrac{1-z}{1+z}=\dfrac{(1-x^2-y^2)-2iy}{(1+x)^2+y^2}\): real part \(\le0\) and imaginary part \(\le0\).

questions.q: If the complex numbers, \(z_1,z_2\) and \(z_3\) represent the vertices of an equilateral triangle such that \(|z_1|=|z_2|=|z_3|\) then \(z_1+z_2+z_3=0\).
questions.sol: The circumcentre is the origin; in an equilateral triangle it coincides with the centroid \(\dfrac{z_1+z_2+z_3}3\).

questions.q: If three complex numbers are in A.P. then they lie on a circle in the complex plane.
questions.sol: If \(z_1,z_2,z_3\) are in A.P., \(z_2\) is the mid-point of \(z_1\) and \(z_3\): the points are collinear.

questions.q: The cube roots of unity when represented on Argand diagram form the vertices of an equilateral triangle
questions.sol: \(1,\omega,\omega^2\) lie on the unit circle with arguments \(0,\frac{2\pi}3,\frac{4\pi}3\), equally spaced.

questions.q: If the expression \(\dfrac{\left[\sin\left(\dfrac x2\right)+\cos\left(\dfrac x2\right)+i\tan(x)\right]}{\left[1+2i\sin\left(\dfrac x2\right)\right]}\) is real, then the set of all possible values of \(x\) is ...........
questions.sol: Multiplying by \(1-2i\sin\frac x2\), the imaginary part is \(\tan x-2\sin\frac x2\left(\sin\frac x2+\cos\frac x2\right)=\tan x-(1-\cos x)-\sin x=0\), i.e. \((1-\cos x)(\tan x-1)=0\).

questions.q: For any two complex numbers \(z_1,z_2\) and any real numbers \(a\) and \(b\), \(|az_1-bz_2|^2+|bz_1+az_2|^2=\) ...........
questions.sol: Expanding with \(|w|^2=w\bar w\), the cross terms \(\mp ab(z_1\bar z_2+\bar z_1z_2)\) cancel.

questions.q: If \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers between \(0\) and \(1\) such that the points \(z_1=a+i\), \(z_2=1+bi\), \(z_3=0\) form an equilateral triangle, then \(a=\) ......... and \(b=\) ........

\(ABCD\) is a rhombus. Its diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at the point \(M\) and satisfy \(BD=2AC\). If the points \(D\) and \(M\) represents the complex numbers \(1+i\) and \(2-i\) respectively, then \(A\) represents the complex number ........ or ...........
questions.sol: \(MD=-1+2i\). \(MA\perp MD\) with \(MA=\frac12MD\): \(A-M=\pm\frac i2(-1+2i)=\mp\left(1+\frac i2\right)\). So \(A=1-\frac{3i}2\) or \(3-\frac i2\).

questions.q: Suppose \(z_1,z_2,z_3\) are the vertices of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle \(|z|=2\). If \(z_1=1+i\sqrt3\) then \(z_2=\) ....... and \(z_3=\) ........
questions.sol: \(z_1=2e^{i\pi/3}\); the other vertices are \(z_1\omega=2e^{i\pi}=-2\) and \(z_1\omega^2=2e^{5i\pi/3}=1-i\sqrt3\).

questions.q: The value of the expression \(1\cdot(2-\omega)(2-\omega^2)+2\cdot(3-\omega)(3-\omega^2)+\ldots+(n-1)\cdot(n-\omega)(n-\omega^2)\), where \(\omega\) is an imaginary cube root of unity, is .....

\(z\ne0\) is a complex number
Column IColumn II
(i) \(\text{Re}\,z=0\)(A) \(\text{Re}\,z^2=0\)
(ii) \(\text{Arg}\,z=\dfrac\pi4\)(B) \(\text{Im}\,z^2=0\)
(C) \(\text{Re}\,z^2=\text{Im}\,z^2\)
questions.sol: (i) \(z=iy\): \(z^2=-y^2\) is real, so \(\text{Im}\,z^2=0\). (ii) \(z^2\) has argument \(\frac\pi2\), so \(\text{Re}\,z^2=0\).

questions.q:
Match the statements in column-I with those in column-II [Note : Here \(z\) takes the values in the complex plane and \(\text{Im}\,z\) and \(\text{Re}\,z\) denote respectively, the imaginary part and the real part of \(z\)]
Column - IColumn - II
(A) The set of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z-i|z||=|z+i|z||\) is contained in or equal to(p) an ellipse with eccentricity \(4/5\)
(B) The set of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z+4|+|z-4|=10\) is contained in or equal to(q) the set of points \(z\) satisfying \(\text{Im}\,z=0\)
(C) If \(|\omega|=2\), then the set of points \(z=\omega-1/\omega\) is contained in or equal to(r) the set of points \(z\) satisfying \(|\text{Im}\,z|\le1\)
(D) If \(|\omega|=1\), then the set of points \(z=\omega+1/\omega\) is contained in or equal to(s) the set of points \(z\) satisfying \(|\text{Re}\,z|\le2\)
(t) the set of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z|\le3\)
questions.sol: (A) \(z\) is equidistant from \(\pm i|z|\), so \(z\) is real: (q), (r). (B) Ellipse with foci \(\pm4\), \(a=5\), \(e=\frac45\): (p). (C) \(\omega=2e^{i\theta}\): \(z=\frac32\cos\theta+\frac52i\sin\theta\), an ellipse with \(e=\frac45\), \(|\text{Re}\,z|\le\frac32\), \(|z|\le\frac52\): (p), (s), (t). (D) \(z=2\cos\theta\) is real with \(|z|\le2\): (q), (r), (s), (t). (The book prints (s) as \(|\text{Re}\,z|\le1\) and its key gives (C) \(\to\) (p) only; the paper has \(|\text{Re}\,z|\le2\).)

questions.q:
Match the statements given in column I with the intervals/union of intervals given in column II.
Column IColumn II
(A) The set \(\left\{\text{Re}\left(\dfrac{2iz}{1-z^2}\right):z\text{ is a complex number, }|z|=1,\ z\ne\pm1\right\}\) is(p) \((-\infty,-1)\cup(1,\infty)\)
(B) The domain of the function \(f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8(3)^{x-2}}{1-3^{2(x-1)}}\right)\) is(q) \((-\infty,0)\cup(0,\infty)\)
(C) If \(f(\theta)=\begin{vmatrix}1&\tan\theta&1\\-\tan\theta&1&\tan\theta\\-1&-\tan\theta&1\end{vmatrix}\), then the set \(\left\{f(\theta):0\le\theta<\dfrac\pi2\right\}\) is(r) \([2,\infty)\)
(D) If \(f(x)=x^{3/2}(3x-10)\), \(x\ge0\), then \(f(x)\) is increasing in(s) \((-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)\)
(t) \((-\infty,0]\cup[2,\infty)\)
questions.sol: (A) \(z=e^{i\theta}\): \(\dfrac{2iz}{1-z^2}=\dfrac{2i}{\bar z-z}=-\dfrac1{\sin\theta}\), giving \((-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)\): (s). (B) With \(t=3^x\): \(-1\le\dfrac{8t}{9-t^2}\le1\) gives \(t\le1\) or \(t\ge9\), i.e. \(x\le0\) or \(x\ge2\): (t). (C) \(f(\theta)=2\sec^2\theta\in[2,\infty)\): (r). (D) \(f'(x)=\frac{15}2\sqrt x(x-2)\ge0\) for \(x\ge2\): (r). (The book key prints (A) \(\to\) (p); the value \(\mp1\) is attained at \(z=\pm i\), so (s) is correct.)

questions.q:
Let \(z_k=\cos\left(\dfrac{2k\pi}{10}\right)+i\sin\left(\dfrac{2k\pi}{10}\right)\); \(k=1,2,\ldots,9\).
List-IList-II
P. For each \(z_k\) there exists a \(z_j\) such that \(z_k\cdot z_j=1\).1. True
Q. There exists a \(k\in\{1,2,\ldots,9\}\) such that \(z_1\cdot z=z_k\) has no solution \(z\) in the set of complex numbers.2. False
R. \(\dfrac{|1-z_1||1-z_2|\ldots|1-z_9|}{10}\) equals3. \(1\)
S. \(1-\sum\limits_{k=1}^9\cos\left(\dfrac{2k\pi}{10}\right)\) equals4. \(2\)
questions.sol: \(z_k\) are the \(10\)th roots of unity other than \(1\). P: \(z_kz_{10-k}=1\), true. Q: \(z=\dfrac{z_k}{z_1}\) always exists, so false. R: \(\prod(1-z_k)=1+1+\ldots+1=10\), ratio \(1\). S: \(\sum\limits_{k=1}^9\cos\dfrac{2k\pi}{10}=-1\), so the value is \(2\).

questions.q:
Let \(z\) be a complex number satisfying \(|z|^3+2z^2+4\bar z-8=0\), where \(\bar z\) denotes the complex conjugate of \(z\). Let the imaginary part of \(z\) be nonzero. Match each entry in List-I to the correct entries in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) \(|z|^2\) is equal to(1) \(12\)
(Q) \(|z-\bar z|^2\) is equal to(2) \(4\)
(R) \(|\bar z|^2+|z+\bar z|^2\) is equal to(3) \(8\)
(S) \(|z+1|^2\) is equal to(4) \(10\)
(5) \(7\)
The correct option is:

Comprehension
Let \(A,B,C\) be three sets of complex numbers as defined below
\(A=\{z:\text{Im}\,z\ge1\}\)
\(B=\{z:|z-2-i|=3\}\)
\(C=\left\{z:\text{Re}((1-i)z)=\sqrt2\right\}\).
The number of elements in the set \(A\cap B\cap C\) is
questions.sol: \(C\) is the line \(x+y=\sqrt2\); \(B\) is a circle with centre \((2,1)\), radius \(3\). The line cuts the circle at \(x=\dfrac{(1+\sqrt2)\pm\sqrt{(1+\sqrt2)(5+\sqrt2)}}2\approx3.18,\,-0.76\) with \(y\approx-1.76,\,2.17\). Only the second point has \(y\ge1\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(A,B,C\) be three sets of complex numbers as defined below
\(A=\{z:\text{Im}\,z\ge1\}\)
\(B=\{z:|z-2-i|=3\}\)
\(C=\left\{z:\text{Re}((1-i)z)=\sqrt2\right\}\).
Let \(z\) be any point in \(A\cap B\cap C\). Then, \(|z+1-i|^2+|z-5-i|^2\) lies between
questions.sol: \(-1+i\) and \(5+i\) are the ends of a diameter of the circle \(B\), and \(z\) is on \(B\), so by Pythagoras the sum is \(6^2=36\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(A,B,C\) be three sets of complex numbers as defined below
\(A=\{z:\text{Im}\,z\ge1\}\)
\(B=\{z:|z-2-i|=3\}\)
\(C=\left\{z:\text{Re}((1-i)z)=\sqrt2\right\}\).
Let \(z\) be any point in \(A\cap B\cap C\) and let \(\omega\) be any point satisfying \(|\omega-2-i|<3\). Then, \(|z|-|\omega|+3\) lies between
questions.sol: \(z\) is on the circle and \(\omega\) inside it, so \(\big||z|-|\omega|\big|\le|z-\omega|<6\) (the diameter). Hence \(-6<|z|-|\omega|<6\) and \(-3<|z|-|\omega|+3<9\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(S=S_1\cap S_2\cap S_3\), where \(S_1=\{z\in C:|z|<4\}\), \(S_2=\left\{z\in C:\text{Im}\left[\dfrac{z-1+\sqrt3i}{1-\sqrt3i}\right]>0\right\}\) and \(S_3=\{z\in C:\text{Re}\,z>0\}\)
Area of \(S=\)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{z-1+\sqrt3i}{1-\sqrt3i}=\dfrac{z(1+\sqrt3i)}4-1\), so \(S_2\) is \(\sqrt3x+y>0\). \(S\) is the sector of the disc \(|z|<4\) from \(-60^\circ\) to \(90^\circ\): area \(\dfrac{150}{360}\cdot16\pi\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(S=S_1\cap S_2\cap S_3\), where \(S_1=\{z\in C:|z|<4\}\), \(S_2=\left\{z\in C:\text{Im}\left[\dfrac{z-1+\sqrt3i}{1-\sqrt3i}\right]>0\right\}\) and \(S_3=\{z\in C:\text{Re}\,z>0\}\)
\(\min\limits_{z\in S}|1-3i-z|=\)
questions.sol: \((1,-3)\) lies outside \(S\) (below the line \(\sqrt3x+y=0\)); the least distance is its perpendicular distance from that line: \(\dfrac{|\sqrt3-3|}2\).

questions.q: If \(z\) is any complex number satisfying \(|z-3-2i|\le2\), then the minimum value of \(|2z-6+5i|\) is
questions.sol: \(|2z-6+5i|=2\left|z-\left(3-\frac52i\right)\right|\). The point \(3-\frac52i\) is at distance \(\frac92\) from the centre \(3+2i\), so the least distance from the disc is \(\frac92-2=\frac52\); twice this is \(5\).

questions.q: Let \(\omega=e^{i\pi/3}\) and \(a,b,c,x,y,z\) be non-zero complex numbers such that \(a+b+c=x\), \(a+b\omega+c\omega^2=y\), \(a+b\omega^2+c\omega=z\). Then the value of \(\dfrac{|x|^2+|y|^2+|z|^2}{|a|^2+|b|^2+|c|^2}\) is
questions.sol: Taking \(\omega\) as a cube root of unity \(\left(e^{2\pi i/3}\right)\), expanding \(|x|^2+|y|^2+|z|^2\) the cross terms carry the factor \(1+\omega+\omega^2=0\), leaving \(3(|a|^2+|b|^2+|c|^2)\). (The paper printed \(\omega=e^{i\pi/3}\), for which the ratio is not constant; the accepted answer is \(3\).)

questions.q: For any integer \(k\), let \(\alpha_k=\cos\left(\dfrac{k\pi}7\right)+i\sin\left(\dfrac{k\pi}7\right)\) where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). The value of the expression \(\dfrac{\sum\limits_{k=1}^{12}|\alpha_{k+1}-\alpha_k|}{\sum\limits_{k=1}^3|\alpha_{4k-1}-\alpha_{4k-2}|}\) is
questions.sol: Consecutive \(\alpha_k\) are adjacent \(14\)th roots of unity, so every \(|\alpha_{k+1}-\alpha_k|=2\sin\dfrac\pi{14}\). Ratio \(=\dfrac{12}3=4\).

questions.q: Let \(\omega\ne1\) be a cube root of unity. Then the minimum of the set \(\{|a+b\omega+c\omega^2|^2:a,b,c\) distinct non-zero integers\(\}\) equals ____.
questions.sol: \(|a+b\omega+c\omega^2|^2=\tfrac12\left[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\right]\); for distinct integers the least is with consecutive values: \(\tfrac12(1+1+4)=3\).

questions.q: For a complex number \(z\), let \(\text{Re}(z)\) denote the real part of \(z\). Let \(S\) be the set of all complex numbers \(z\) satisfying \(z^4-|z|^4=4iz^2\), where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). Then the minimum possible value of \(|z_1-z_2|^2\), where \(z_1,z_2\in S\) with \(\text{Re}(z_1)>0\) and \(\text{Re}(z_2)<0\), is _____
questions.sol: \(z^2(z^2-\bar z^2)=4iz^2\), so \(z=0\) or \(z^2-\bar z^2=4ixy=4i\), i.e. \(xy=1\). The closest points on the two branches are \((1,1)\) and \((-1,-1)\): distance\(^2=8\).

questions.q: Let \(z\) be a complex number with non-zero imaginary part. If \(\dfrac{2+3z+4z^2}{2-3z+4z^2}\) is a real number, then the value of \(|z|^2\) is ______.
questions.sol: The fraction is \(1+\dfrac{6z}{2-3z+4z^2}\), so \(\dfrac{2-3z+4z^2}z=\dfrac2z-3+4z\) is real. Its imaginary part \(y\left(4-\dfrac2{|z|^2}\right)=0\) with \(y\ne0\) gives \(|z|^2=\dfrac12\).

questions.q: Let \(\bar z\) denote the complex conjugate of a complex number \(z\) and let \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). In the set of complex numbers, the number of distinct roots of the equation \(\bar z-z^2=i(\bar z+z^2)\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(\bar z(1-i)=z^2(1+i)\) gives \(\bar z=iz^2\). Moduli: \(|z|=0\) or \(1\). \(z=0\) is a root; for \(|z|=1\), \(\bar z=\frac1z\) gives \(z^3=-i\): three roots. Total \(4\).

questions.q: Let \(A=\left\{\dfrac{1967+1686i\sin\theta}{7-3i\cos\theta}:\theta\in\mathbb R\right\}\). If \(A\) contains exactly one positive integer \(n\), then the value of \(n\) is
questions.sol: Multiplying by \(7+3i\cos\theta\): the imaginary part \(5901\cos\theta+11802\sin\theta=0\) gives \(\tan\theta=-\frac12\), so \(\sin\theta\cos\theta=-\frac25\), \(\cos^2\theta=\frac45\). Real part \(=\dfrac{13769-5058\sin\theta\cos\theta}{49+9\cos^2\theta}=\dfrac{15792.2}{56.2}=281\).

questions.q: Let \(A_1,A_2,A_3,\ldots,A_8\) be the vertices of a regular octagon that lie on a circle of radius \(2\). Let \(P\) be a point on the circle and let \(PA_i\) denote the distance between the points \(P\) and \(A_i\) for \(i=1,2,\ldots,8\). If \(P\) varies over the circle, then the maximum value of the product \(PA_1\cdot PA_2\ldots PA_8\), is
questions.sol: Taking the vertices as the roots of \(z^8=2^8\): \(\prod PA_i=|z^8-2^8|\) with \(|z|=2\), which is at most \(2^8+2^8=512\) (attained when \(z^8=-2^8\)).

questions.q:
For a non-zero complex number \(z\), let \(\arg(z)\) denote the principal argument of \(z\), with \(-\pi<\arg(z)\le\pi\). Let \(\omega\) be the cube root of unity for which \(0<\arg(\omega)<\pi\). Let \(\alpha=\arg\left(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{2025}(-\omega)^n\right)\).
Then the value of \(\dfrac{3\alpha}\pi\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(-\omega=e^{-i\pi/3}\) is a primitive sixth root of unity, so every six consecutive terms add to \(0\). \(2025=6\cdot337+3\): the sum is \((-\omega)+\omega^2-1=-1-\sqrt3i\), whose argument is \(-\dfrac{2\pi}3\).

questions.q:
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the distinct roots of the equation \(x^2+x+1=0\), then the quadratic equation with roots \(\dfrac1{(\alpha+1)^{2026}}\) and \(\dfrac1{(\beta+1)^{2026}}\) is(1) \(x^2+x+1=0\)
(Q) If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the distinct roots of the equation \(x^2+x+1=0\), then the quadratic equation with roots \(\dfrac1{(\alpha+1)^{2027}}\) and \(\dfrac1{(\beta+1)^{2027}}\) is(2) \(x^2-x+1=0\)
(R) If \(\gamma\) and \(\delta\) are the distinct roots of the equation \(x^2-x+1=0\), then the value of \(\dfrac1{(\gamma-1)^{2026}}+\dfrac1{(\delta-1)^{2026}}\) is(3) \(x^2+x-1=0\)
(S) If \(p\) and \(r\) are the distinct roots of the equation \(x^2+x-1=0\), then the value of \(\dfrac1{(p+1)^3}+\dfrac1{(r+1)^3}\) is(4) \(-1\)
(5) \(-4\)
questions.sol: \(\alpha,\beta=\omega,\omega^2\), so \(\alpha+1=-\omega^2\), \(\beta+1=-\omega\). (P) Even power: the roots are \(\omega,\omega^2\): \(x^2+x+1=0\). (Q) Odd power: \(-\omega,-\omega^2\): \(x^2-x+1=0\). (R) \(\gamma,\delta=-\omega,-\omega^2\), \(\gamma-1=\omega^2\), \(\delta-1=\omega\): \(\omega+\omega^2=-1\). (S) \(u=p+1\), \(v=r+1\) are roots of \(y^2-y-1=0\): \(\dfrac{u^3+v^3}{(uv)^3}=\dfrac{1+3}{-1}=-4\).
